claims.text: the snapshot's recorded head ... is not a git object name (at least _MIN_ABBREV hex characters), so it cannot be checked against the tree it describes
claims.why: The condition that triggers this return is not shown; _MIN_ABBREV is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: git could not report HEAD; freshness unknown, failing open
claims.why: Code returns fresh=True and actual_head=None when actual_head is None or 'unknown'.

claims.text: actual.startswith(recorded) is the containment that can be true. Testing the reverse would let a shorter actual satisfy a longer recorded value, which is not a relationship any git abbreviation produces.
claims.why: The code uses actual_head.startswith(recorded) and not the reverse.

claims.text: the snapshot was generated against {recorded[:12]} but HEAD is {actual_head[:12]}
Pure: no writes, no clock, no network.
claims.why: The function body does not contain any I/O operations visible in this chunk, but full verification requires seeing all imports and calls.

claims.text: reach_report and switch_report may be injected by a caller that already built them (daedalus map does, and that is the point: the page and the gate are then provably looking at the same analysis, not at two that happen to agree). index is only forwarded to reach for its structural cross-check.
claims.why: Code checks if reach_report is None and if switch_report is None, and builds them if not provided. index is passed to reach_mod.analyse.

claims.text: The state also records WHICH TREE it was derived from (repo_state). It belongs here rather than in the writer because it is a property of the scan, and because a state that cannot say what it scanned is the exact hole this module spent a release closing on the hand-written side.
claims.why: The state dict includes 'repo_state' key with result of repo_state(root, probe_dirty=probe_dirty).

claims.text: TEST ONLY is a property of an UNREACHED module, not of an island specifically. Scoping it to islands meant a shim or an unknown whose only importer was a test could not be described that way at all.
claims.why: test_only is built from unreached_facts (which includes islands, unknown, shims) filtered by m.tested_by.

claims.text: Two engines disagreeing about the import graph. reach REPORTS these and refuses to merge them (see reach.analyse); the gate is where a disagreement that persists across a commit becomes somebody's problem.
claims.why: The comment refers to reach.analyse, which is not in this chunk. The code does use reach_report.index_extra_edges.

claims.text: An absent API key is not a dark feature. The feature it belongs to is documented and merely unconfigured -- daedalus doctor already reports it, and an architecture gate is a poor place to enumerate which secrets a machine is missing. secret is the switch engine's own classification, so this is a filter over one answer, not a second opinion about what a switch is.
claims.why: Code skips switches with sw.kind == 'secret' when building dark dict.

claims.text: A module the scanner could not parse contributes nothing to either engine's answer, which makes it a hole in the map that used to be filled by a bare continue. It is a finding, not a shrug.
claims.why: Code builds unparsable set from both reach_report.unparsable and switch_report.unparsable, and includes it in state.

claims.text: The honest total: every module on disk that no entry point reaches, whatever reach called it. It is the number the page has to add up to, and it is what 'islands=7' used to hide.
claims.why: unreached count is len(islands) + len(unknown_mods) + len(shims).

claims.text: Fail closed: anything we cannot fully validate is kept, marked with a problem, and suppresses nothing. A typo in an acceptance must never be the thing that makes an island invisible.
claims.why: The function always returns a list, and malformed entries are included with a problem string.

claims.text: today binds the horizon to the CALENDAR. Without it the only rule is until - since <= MAX_HORIZON_DAYS, which a pair of dates in 2999 satisfies while suppressing forever; the cap measured the acceptance against itself and nothing measured it against now. Omitting today keeps the date-shape and horizon checks and skips only that one, so a caller that genuinely has no clock (--accept validating a candidate before writing it) still gets everything else.
claims.why: Code checks if today is not None before comparing d_since > today.

claims.text: Which tree the SNAPSHOT was generated against, versus the one just scanned. Reported, never blocking: a baseline taken one commit ago is not a defect, and a gate that goes red on every commit is a gate people switch off. The consumers that RANK WORK out of these lists are the ones that must fail closed on it -- see snapshot_freshness.
claims.why: The claim references snapshot_freshness, which is not in this chunk. The freshness field is present.

observations.what: The _freshness function returns dictionaries with specific keys; it handles cases where recorded is not a valid git object name, where actual_head is None/unknown, and where actual_head starts with recorded or not.
The scan function builds a comprehensive state dict including counts, modules lists, and site mappings; it imports reach_mod and switches_mod inside the function.
parse_acceptances validates each entry's fields and returns a sorted list of Acceptance objects; it performs date parsing and horizon checks.
DriftItem and DriftReport are dataclasses with properties and methods; DriftReport has a blocking property that filters items by non-blocking kinds and accepted status.
